arxiv-2206-03923.title: Sequential Density Estimation via Nonlinear Continuous Weighted Finite Automata
arxiv-2206-03923.creator: Tianyu Li, Bogdan Mazoure, Guillaume Rabusseau
arxiv-2206-03923.description: Abstract Weighted finite automata (WFAs) have been widely applied in many fields. One of the classic problems for WFAs is probability distribution estimation over sequences of discrete symbols. Although WFAs have been extended to deal with continuous input data, namely continuous WFAs (CWFAs) ( Li et al.

arxiv-2308-08169.title: Enhancing Performance on Seen and Unseen Dialogue Scenarios using Retrieval-Augmented End-to-End Task-Oriented System
arxiv-2308-08169.creator: Jianguo Zhang Stephen Roller Kun Qian Zhiwei Liu Rui Meng, Shelby Heinecke Huan Wang Silvio Savarese Caiming Xiong
arxiv-2308-08169.description: Abstract End-to-end task-oriented dialogue (TOD) systems have achieved promising performance by leveraging sophisticated natural language understanding and natural language generation capabilities of pre-trained models. This work enables the TOD systems with more flexibility through a simple cache. The cache provides the flexibility to dynamically update the TOD systems and handle both existing and unseen dialogue scenarios.

arxiv-2402-17546.title: CoCoA : CBT-based Conversational Counseling Agent using Memory Specialized in Cognitive Distortions and Dynamic Prompt
arxiv-2402-17546.creator: Suyeon Lee, Jieun Kang, Harim Kim, Kyoung-Mee Chung, Dongha Lee, Jinyoung Yeo, Department of Artificial Intelligence, Yonsei University, Department of Psychology, Yonsei University {isuy.groot, likemika605}@gmail.com{harim.k, kmchung, donalee, jinyeo}@yonsei.ac.kr
arxiv-2402-17546.description: Abstract The demand for conversational agents that provide mental health care is consistently increasing. In this work, we develop a psychological counseling agent, referred to as CoCoA that applies Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) techniques to identify and address cognitive distortions inherent in the client’s statements.

arxiv-2406-16655.title: Large Language Models Are Cross-Lingual Knowledge-Free Reasoners
arxiv-2406-16655.creator: Peng Hu, Sizhe Liu, Changjiang Gao, Xin Huang, Xue Han, Junlan Feng, Chao Deng, Shujian Huang
arxiv-2406-16655.description: Abstract Large Language Models have demonstrated impressive reasoning capabilities across multiple languages. However, the relationship between capabilities in different languages is less explored. In this work, we decompose the process of reasoning tasks into two separated components: knowledge retrieval and knowledge-free reasoning, and analyze the relationship between cross-lingual transferability and these two components.

arxiv-2502-16423.title: Unified Prompt Attack Against Text-to-Image Generation Models
arxiv-2502-16423.creator: Duo Peng, Qiuhong Ke, Mark He Huang, Ping Hu, Jun Liu
arxiv-2502-16423.description: Abstract Text-to-Image (T2I) models have advanced significantly, but their growing popularity raises security concerns due to their potential to generate harmful images. To address these issues, we propose UPAM, a novel framework to evaluate the robustness of T2I models from an attack perspective.

arxiv-2505-11638.title: Accelerating Natural Gradient Descent for PINNs with Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra Thanks: Corresponding author: Ivan Bioli
arxiv-2505-11638.creator: Ivan Bioli †,‡, Carlo Marcati §, Giancarlo Sangalli †,¶
arxiv-2505-11638.description: Abstract . Natural Gradient Descent (NGD) has emerged as a promising optimization algorithm for training neural network-based solvers for partial differential equations (PDEs), such as Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). However, its practical use is often limited by the high computational cost of solving linear systems involving the Gramian matrix.

arxiv-2512-08096.title: Selling Privacy in Blockchain Transactions
arxiv-2512-08096.creator: Georgios Chionas Olga Gorelkina University of Liverpool UM6P g.chionas@liverpool.ac.uk olga.gorelkina@um6p.ma Piotr Krysta Rida Laraki Augusta University UM6P pkrysta@augusta.edu rida.laraki@um6p.ma
arxiv-2512-08096.description: Abstract We study methods to enhance privacy in blockchain transactions from an economic angle. We consider mechanisms for privacy-aware users whose utility depends not only on the outcome of the mechanism but also negatively on the exposure of their economic preferences. Specifically, we study two auction-theoretic settings with privacy-aware users.

europmc-pmc6539237.title: The Possible Role of the Microbiota-Gut-Brain-Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorder.
europmc-pmc6539237.creator: Srikantha P, Mohajeri MH.
europmc-pmc6539237.description: New research points to a possible link between autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and the gut microbiota as many autistic children have co-occurring gastrointestinal problems. This review focuses on specific alterations of gut microbiota mostly observed in autistic patients....

Plus-end-tracking proteins (+TIPs) are localized at the fast-growing, or plus end, of microtubules, and link microtubule ends to cellular structures. One of the best studied +TIPs is EB1, which forms comet-like structures at the tips of growing microtubules. The molecular mechani

pmc-10691395.title: Biological and Adhesive Properties of an Autologous Protein-Based Fibrin Sealant for Ophthalmological Applications
pmc-10691395.creator: Eduardo Anitua, Francisco Muruzabal, Roberto Prado, Ander Pino, Roberto Tierno, Mairobi Persinal-Medina, Mohammad H. Alkhraisat, Jesús Merayo-Lloves
pmc-10691395.description: PurposeThe aim of this study was to evaluate the biological and adhesive properties of a new autologous sealant based on plasma rich in growth factors (PRGF), named E-Sealant.MethodsConventional PRGF and a commercial fibrin sealant (Tisseel) were included as controls. The hematological and protein content of E-Sealant was determined. Its bioactivity and biocompatibility were tested for human keratocytes (HKs).

pmc-11406091.title: Zearalenone-induced hepatointestinal toxicity in laying hens: unveiling the role of gut microbiota and fecal metabolites
pmc-11406091.creator: Lingling Wang, Zifeng Deng, Jieying Huang, Tingyuan Li, Jun Jiang, Wence Wang, Yu Sun, Yiqun Deng
pmc-11406091.description: Zearalenone (ZEN), a mycotoxin produced by Fusarium species, is known for its reproductive toxicity as an estrogen analogue. However, there are limited knowledge about its hepatointestinal toxicity, as well as the role that gut microbiota and metabolites play in this process.

pmc-11639994.title: Plant-Based Meat Alternatives Predicted by Theory of Planned Behavior Among Midwest Undergraduates
pmc-11639994.creator: Rachel H. Luong, Donna M. Winham, Mack C. Shelley, Abigail A. Glick
pmc-11639994.description: Plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs) such as the Impossible Burger® imitate animal meat appearance, taste, feel, and texture. Part of their consumer appeal are the views that PBMAs are more environmentally friendly, reduce inhumane treatment of animals, and/or have preferred nutritional attributes. College-educated adults are one of the larger markets for these products.

pmc-11696401.title: Synthesis and Characterization of NaX Zeolite from Coal Gangue and Its Efficacy in Cd and Pb Remediation in Water and Soil
pmc-11696401.creator: Zhibing Chang, Yinuo Yan, Lu Bai, Nan Guo, Zhenguo Xing, Chunwei Lu
pmc-11696401.description: Alkaline fusion is a pivotal process influencing the cost of synthesizing zeolite from coal gangue. This study examined the effects of alkaline fusion temperature (X1), treatment duration (X2) and the NaOH/coal gangue weight ratio (X3) on the composition and properties of the products, as well as their adsorption capacities for Cd2+ (qe,Cd) and Pb2+ (qe,Pb).

pmc-11709389.title: A novel coumarin derivative treatment ameliorates neuroinflammation and cognitive functions in the ICV‐STZ‐induced rat model of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11709389.creator: PRAJJWAL SHARMA
pmc-11709389.description: BackgroundNeuroinflammation has gained substantial attention for its involvement in the progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD).MethodRecently, it was discovered that platelets, which make up 90% of the circulatory Aβ, encourage the development of AD. Therefore, we hypothesized to use a novel coumarin derivative PS21HKR, which is believed to possess anti‐platelet and anti‐inflammatory properties for the treatment of AD.

pmc-12577330.title: Efficacy of vitamin C in COVID-19 management: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12577330.creator: Shuyi Zhou, Shijie Gao, Yujie Fang, Na Zhang, Guansheng Ma
pmc-12577330.description: BackgroundCOVID-19 has posed a global burden, with vitamin C considered a potential treatment due to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. However, its efficacy remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the impact of vitamin C supplementation on COVID-19 patients.

pmc-13061630.title: Competitive interactions shape mammalian brain network dynamics and computation
pmc-13061630.creator: Andrea I. Luppi, Yonatan Sanz Perl, Jakub Vohryzek, Hana Ali, Pedro A. M. Mediano, Fernando E. Rosas, Filip Milisav, Laura E. Suárez, Silvia Gini, Daniel Gutierrez-Barragan, Yohan Yee, Seán Froudist-Walsh, Alessandro Gozzi, Bratislav Misic, Gustavo Deco, Morten L. Kringelbach
pmc-13061630.description: How does brain network architecture balance cooperation and competition between distributed circuits? Here we use computational whole-brain modeling to examine the dynamical and computational relevance of cooperative and competitive interactions in the mammalian connectome. Across human, macaque and mouse, we show that to faithfully reproduce brain activity, model architecture consistently combines modular cooperative interactions with diffuse, long-range competitive interactions.
